title: Progressive standby warmup and probabilistic failover orchestrator with model-variant safety net
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Problem: We need an orchestrator that can detect region degradation early and promote a standby region with minimal customer impact. Existing controllers either flip traffic abruptly (risking tail-latency spikes) or require manual priming of standby capacity. Goal: implement a progressive standby warmup flow driven by probabilistic health scoring and safe model-variant fallbacks. The orchestrator will (1) compute a readiness score for candidate standby pools using synthetic probes + shadowed production samples, (2) ramp traffic using a staged, percentage-based cutover that adjusts batching/cache knobs to meet token-latency SLOs, and (3) if the primary model exhibits regressions under degraded infra, automatically route a fraction of traffic to vetted model-variants with quality gating. This ticket covers design, implementation of probe types, readiness scoring, ramp controller, model-variant routing policy, and end-to-end tests.
success_metrics: Cutover time to 95% traffic under automated flow <= 120s (excluding capacity spinup)
User-facing 99th percentile token latency increase during failover <= 15%
Fallback model routing reduces error-rate regressions by >= 60% in simulated infra degradation
Readiness false-positive rate < 2% over 30-day rollout window
Automated cutovers require manual intervention < 1% of cases during canary
acceptance_criteria: Readiness scoring service emits per-pool readiness_score (0.0-1.0) with documented inputs
Ramp controller supports staged cutover percentages (0,1,5,20,50,100) with configurable dwell times
Model-variant policy can route traffic per-customer and per-route to fallback variants with QA gating
Integration test simulating regional network degradation shows controller promotes standby and meets latency SLOs
Observability: dashboards for readiness score, staged ramp progress, and per-variant quality regressions are created
Runbook updated with automated rollback and manual takeover steps
implementation_notes: Probe types: synthetic prompt latency/quality probes, KV cache-prefix priming probes, and shadowed sample validation against golden prompts
Readiness inputs: node health, model-inference-p95 latency, cache-hit ratio, prefetch success rate, recent eval pass-rate, and deploy-version parity
Score composition: weighted sum with tunable thresholds; use exponential decay for older observations to prefer recent behavior
Ramp logic: percentage-based traffic assignment with dynamic adjustment if SLOs are violated during dwell; backoff to previous stage on regression
Model-variant gating: canary traffic for new variant limited to 0.5-2% with automatic expand/rollback based on quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE-ish + custom prompt evals and hallucination detectors)
KV cache prefill: on promotion, prefetch top-N popular prefixes from primary's telemetry into standby caches to reduce early cold-start latency
Batching adjustments: decrease max_batch_size in first stages to reduce tail under variable load; increase as latency stabilizes
Routing tie-breakers: prefer same-tier capacity, then lower-cost tier if latency within 10%
Audit: emit events for each stage change, model-variant switch, and readiness score crossing thresholds to the audit log with timestamps and contributing signals
Config surface: readiness threshold, stage dwell times, batch knob overrides, fallback variant list, and quorum size for activation must be configurable per-customer and per-route
Safety: incorporate circuit-breaker so aggressive retries or sustained queue growth halts ramp and triggers model-variant fallback path

progress_updates: 2026-02-26: RFC posted for readiness scoring. Feedback requested from SRE and Runtime teams.
2026-03-02: Prototype readiness service emits synthetic probe telemetry to /metrics endpoint. Early score computed as weighted average (latency, cache-hit, eval-pass).
2026-03-05: Integration spike shows staged ramp logic requires rate-limiter coordination to avoid warmup storms; added token-bucket gating.
2026-03-09: Model-variant policy design approved by PM; decided to reuse existing rollout service for gating and metrics collection.
2026-03-12: E2E failure simulation plan drafted; SRE will run first simulation next week in staging with shadow traffic replay corpus.
review_feedback: PM (E. Carter): please add customer-specific overrides for enterprise tenants that pin variant lists and hold fixed ramp schedules.
SRE (N. Okafor): ensure prefill does not exceed standby memory quotas; add backpressure controls and quota accounting.
Security (L. Gomez): audit events must include prefetch keys hashed; do not log raw prompt texts in probes to avoid PII leaks.
Runtime (A. Flores): recommend exposing a batch-size override as a hint rather than hard cap so backend kernels can make final decision.
testing_plan: Unit tests for score computation with synthetic signal permutations
Integration test: staged ramp in local cluster with canary traffic validation
Chaos test: simulate 20% packet loss to primary region and validate automated promotion completes without manual intervention
Quality test: run 1000 golden prompts through fallback variant and ensure quality regression metrics remain within threshold
Load test: exercise prefill path with 5M prefix keys capped by quota to validate throttling
rollback_plan: Immediate: abort ramp and revert routing weights to last stable stage
Short-term: disable model-variant routing and route all traffic to primary if healthy
Manual: if standby performance degrades, run manual capacity diagnostics and invoke DR runbook to spin additional nodes
Postmortem: collect readiness signals and audit events to compute root cause and adjust scoring weights
notes: Avoid using "warm-standby" in UI copy; prefer 'standby warmup' to reduce confusion with dedicated warm pools terminology.
We should instrument cost delta during ramp to ensure we don't violate reserved capacity budgets for Dedicated customers.
